Six things get lost between platforms.

Prop semantics

Three APIs for one component

Call sites aren’t portable, and the docs fork.

State coverage

A state quietly goes missing

It exists on web, not on Android. Nobody notices until a designer opens the build.

Motion feel

Curves get eyeballed

Durations are copied; springs are re-tuned by hand and read differently.

Accessibility intent

ARIA doesn’t translate

Native semantics are reinvented per component, inconsistently.

Token bindings

One hardcoded hex

The rebrand ships broken on exactly one target.

Interaction logic

Hover has no touch twin

Each team invents a mapping, and they don’t agree.

New workflow:
a code-first,
tooling-based approach.

ToNative is a workflow and a tool that hands every platform the design’s decisions, not a picture of them. No guessing, no drift, no waiting on design.

Build it once in code.
Hand every platform the same spec.

1 · Build in code

<Counter value={3} max={99} />
−3+
min 0max 99step 1hold repeats

In code the component actually works: you can press it, hold it, hit its limits. Behaviour is shown, not described.

→

2 · Capture as a contract

counter.contract.json

{
  "props":  { "min": 0, "max": 99 },
  "states": ["rest", "pressed", "max"],
  "motion": { "pop": "110%, 100ms" },
  "access": { "role": "spinbutton" }
}

Describe it as data: one contract that holds every detail.

→

3 · Output platform specs

ios.jsoniOS team builds from this
android.jsonAndroid team builds from this

Generate a spec file for each platform. Each team builds from its own.

Every team builds from the same written decisions. Nothing is left to guess.

From Storybook into the tool.

Built and reviewed in Storybook. Quick to spin up, so you see right away if it’s built correctly.

Handed to ToNative by its folder. Code and styles are read; anything missing becomes a question.

An example, built on iOS.

Counter.tsx→ios.json→SwiftUI

  • the same props: value, min, max, step
  • the same options: frozen, full width
  • the same labels for screen readers

Built on iOS from the spec alone. No handoff call, a tighter review loop.

iOS · built from the spec

It reads the code. You see every decision.

  • Read-only by design. The only fields you can edit are the few that exist nowhere in the code.
  • One component, eight views: props, appearance, events, motion, accessibility, what’s left to the platform, the specs.
  • Its docs are generated from the source they describe, so they can’t go stale.
